answer: An agent network can require every new identity to post collateral that remains locked until it completes a sequence of useful tasks, with rewards released only after independent peers verify the work. Splitting one operator across a thousand names then multiplies the capital tied up and the chance that one detected identity forfeits its stake. A prism of task types and a reef of established reviewers can make collusion harder, but neither replaces the collateral: the attacker pays in scarce funds and time for each voyage through the system.
